fileDigest.description: SHA-256 over the raw bytes of the file, rendered as 'sha256:' plus 64 lowercase hex characters.

inputSetDigest.description: Composite digest over a role's input set. Select every inputs[] entry with the target role; sort them ascending by the UTF-8 bytes of inputs[].path; render one line per entry as the 64 lowercase hex characters of its sha256, two ASCII spaces, the repo-relative POSIX path, and a single LF; concatenate the lines as UTF-8 and SHA-256 the result. This is byte-identical to piping GNU sha256sum output for the same files, in the same order, through sha256sum again.
inputSetDigest.sortOrder: ascending by UTF-8 bytes of the repo-relative path
inputSetDigest.reproduce: LC_ALL=C sha256sum <paths in sorted order> | sha256sum

canonicalJsonDigest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON serialization of this manifest's authPolicy object: object members sorted ascending by the code points of their names, no insignificant whitespace, ',' and ':' separators, strings escaped only for '\\', '"', and the JSON control-character escapes, and non-ASCII characters emitted literally as UTF-8. Numbers are not permitted anywhere inside authPolicy so the serialization never depends on a numeric formatter.

inputs.purpose: Canonical vector seed: base schema, honua.seed_metadata_v2_compat_snapshot, service test_service, canonical layer 0, ten read fixtures, and isolated WFS-T mutation layers 10-12.
Render/raster seed: service browser_compat with Point/LineString/Polygon layers 2000/2001/2002 and one deterministic 64x64 single-band raster on layer 2000.
Authorization seed: the public/org/private Portal tier ladder (services portal_public/portal_org/portal_private, layers 3000/3001/3002).
Certification auth breadth seed: protected vector and WMS mirrors used for API-key and OIDC bearer parity against the anonymous baselines.
Applier that materializes the YAML seed files; the YAML inputs have no meaning independent of it, so it is part of the fixture input set.
Definition of which seed files are applied, and in which order, for the client-compat matrix. Adding or removing a fixture input changes this file and therefore fixtureRevision.
Declared server-configuration input: server mode, runtime and database images, environment, base URL, canonical service/layer identity, and the pinned setup-action revision.

metadataGraph.notes: The snapshot is deterministic: generatedAt is a frozen literal and every collection is aggregated in a declared sort order, so re-running the seed against the same inputs reproduces the same document and the same etag.

ordering.featureIdAssignment: features.objectid is a BIGSERIAL. PostgreSQL evaluates the seed's VALUES scan in declaration order, so on a freshly created database the ids run alpha=1 through lambda=10, and the insert is guarded by WHERE NOT EXISTS on layer 0 so re-applying the seed never renumbers or duplicates rows. Lanes must nevertheless address features by attribute (name, status) and treat objectid as stable-but-opaque; no case id asserts a literal id value.
ordering.pagination: Deterministic paging requires an explicit sort on objectid; PAGE_SIZE 3 over 10 features yields pages of 3, 3, 3, 1.
ordering.metadataCollectionOrder: Resources and storage bindings are aggregated ORDER BY their id; publications are aggregated ORDER BY service slug, layer id, then a fixed per-publication-type rank (image, ogc, feature, map, stac).
ordering.wfsFeatureTypeOrder: Feature types are ordered by storage layer id, then publication layer index, then resource name (case-insensitive).
ordering.portalItemIdentity: Portal item ids are derived from the Metadata v2 graph at request time and are not stable literals. Clients must discover them through /sharing/rest/search and must not hard-code them; the stable identity is the service name and its projected access tier.

protocolProjections.serviceProjection: single shared OGC API Features root; the v1 service name is not part of the path

protocolProjections.notes: The local type name is derived from the layer name by lowercasing and collapsing non-alphanumeric runs to underscores; the feature-id format is derived from the stored-query parser and is not asserted by any 2026.1 case id.

protocolProjections.layerIdentity: the storage layer id rendered as a string
protocolProjections.notes: There is no unscoped /wms route: WMS is always service-scoped. The js lane uses the /ogc/services form and the js-cesium lane uses the MapServer form.

protocolProjections.layerIdentity: the storage layer id rendered as a string
protocolProjections.notes: There is no unscoped /wmts route: WMTS is always service-scoped.
Vector tiles are the mvt projection of the OGC API Tiles surface; the three browser_compat layers supply the point, line, and polygon symbology facets.
The 2026.1 OData certification producer runs in-process against tests/seed/odata.yaml; see gap odata-surface-uses-separate-seed.

vectorSeedCoverage.evidence: test_service layer 0 seeds nine POINT geometries.
browser_compat layer 2001 seeds two LINESTRING geometries.
browser_compat layer 2002 seeds two POLYGON geometries.
The tenth feature (lambda) is seeded with a NULL geometry, so nine of ten rows carry geometry.
The description attribute is NULL on alpha, delta, eta, and lambda.
count is a monotone integer 1..10 and ratio a double 1.25..12.50; eo:cloud_cover is a double 2.0..95.0 with one NULL.
active alternates true/false across the ten rows.
created_at (timestamptz), event_date (date), and event_time (time) are seeded on every row.
uid carries ten distinct UUID literals.
tags (string array) and numbers (integer array) are seeded as JSON arrays on every row.
status = 'active' selects exactly five rows on every run.
The subset bbox (-122.495, 37.705, -122.455, 37.735) selects exactly the first three points.
objectid is assigned in seed order and page size 3 partitions the ten features as 3/3/3/1.

The py-owslib lane certifies WFS-T insert, update, and delete against dedicated fixture-owned scratch layers 10-12; mutation of canonical layer 0 and Create/Update/Delete/Sync coverage through other advertised protocol surfaces remain uncertified.

raster.description: One deterministic 64x64 single-band 8BUI raster with every pixel set to 180, anchored at (-122.45, 37.80) with a 0.00109375 degree pixel, plus a matching honua.raster_statistics row (min=max=mean=180, stddev=0, 4096 valid pixels).

styleAndRender.description: Render facets are certified from the three browser_compat geometry-type layers through the mvt and image surfaces. No stored style document exists: every seeded resource declares an empty styleResourceIds array.

stac.description: The stac-api service projection publishes collection 0 over the same ten seeded features, with eo:cloud_cover as a real queryable numeric field and created_at as the temporal field.

gpBuffer.reason: No active or bounded 2026.1 client lane binds the GPServer surface: no lane in the certification matrix declares a gpserver protocol, so a GP buffer fixture is not part of the frozen 2026.1 core.

mapAndDashboard.description: The Portal/Sharing facade projects the three tiered services as Feature/Map/Image Service items, which is the map-catalogue input the 2026.1 arcgis-stub lane consumes.

authPolicy.secretHandling: This manifest names environment variables, headers, principals, and roles only. The single literal it carries is the well-known non-production bootstrap key value that already appears in docker/client-compat/compose.yml and tests/python/shared/canonical_fixture.py; it is never a production credential and must never be reused outside the client-compat fixture.

mechanisms.notes: The bootstrap key carries no permission claims, so AdminApiKeyPermission treats it as full admin (read and write). Scoped keys (admin:read, admin:write, ops:read) are supported by the server but no scoped key is provisioned by this fixture.
The local lane mints deterministic HS256 JWTs against the server's symmetric test-validation seam; no external identity provider is contacted.
AdminPortalCredentialVerifier maps the admin principal to roles [admin] only. No principal in this fixture ever holds portal-admin.

Anonymous access is granted where the seeded accessPolicy sets allowAnonymous true, and refused everywhere else. The dev-auth bypass is disabled because the stack runs ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production.

roles.notes: Bootstrap admin role projected by the API-key handler and the portal credential verifier.
Required by portal_private.accessPolicy.allowedRoles. Deliberately granted to no principal, so the private tier is the denial arm of the role ladder.

profiles.notes: test_service, browser_compat, and portal_public set allowAnonymous true; the admin surface and portal_org/portal_private refuse anonymous callers.

The OWSLib and GeoPandas core reads present X-API-Key or an OIDC bearer to protected mirror services and assert semantic parity with the anonymous baselines; the Portal lane exchanges the bootstrap secret for a named-user token.
A wrong X-API-Key value yields 401 with the ApiKey challenge; generateToken with wrong credentials yields the Esri error envelope without leaking a token.
The Python certification helper mints a correctly signed JWT whose exp is in the past and asserts the protocol-specific denial status, challenge, and error body.

portal_private requires role portal-admin, which the admin principal never holds, so the denial condition exists in the fixture; no 2026.1 case id asserts that the private tier stays hidden from a token holder.
The client-compat stack seeds a single tenant, so no second tenant exists to be denied.
Only one principal (admin) is provisioned, so a proposer and a distinct approver cannot be distinguished.
Entitlement-bound access is realized only by the licensed release overlay (ArcGIS Pro, BI clients); the unlicensed local profile has no entitlement to present.

deploymentProfiles.description: The shared unlicensed profile: source-built server on the docker/client-compat network, PostGIS 16-3.4, Redis, HTTP only.
The release overlay: the exact candidate container image rather than a source build, behind TLS, with the same seeds applied by the same applier.
overlayRules: Additive only: the overlay may pin the candidate image digest and enable TLS, and may not change any seeded identity, count, extent, or access policy.
fixtureRevision, serverConfigRevision, and authPolicyRevision are carried through unchanged; a differing value is drift, not an overlay.
CERT-CONN-02 becomes applicable here because the transport is TLS.

deploymentProfiles.description: The licensed overlay for entitlement-bound clients (ArcGIS Pro/arcpy, Excel, Power BI, Tableau) running against the exact candidate.
overlayRules: Additive only: licensed lanes bind the same seeded identities and the same auth policy, plus an entitlement the unlicensed profile cannot present.
Licensed evidence must be fresh for the release run and content-addressed to the same candidate image digest.
The licensed overlay may not substitute its own seed for the canonical fixture; a lane that needs a different seed declares a governed exception instead.

applicableButUnexecuted.rule: A case an active lane declares applicable but does not execute is emitted as skip and treated as a failure by the strict baseline diff. It is never absent from the envelope and never counted as a pass.

unsupported.rule: A case a lane cannot structurally execute is emitted as not-applicable and must carry a reason drawn from the governed vocabulary. An ungoverned or empty reason is a gate failure.

placeholderBaseline.definition: An envelope in which no common-core result carries the status pass or fail.
placeholderBaseline.rule: All-skip and all-not-applicable baselines are rejected; a lane cannot be registered without a real envelope.

missingReceiptBinding.rule: An envelope that omits a required receipt field, or binds a revision this manifest does not publish, cannot claim canonical-fixture provenance.

missingEvidence.rule: A required lane that produces no envelope at all fails the tier; absence is never treated as a pass.

tiers.pr: Validate this manifest, its schema, its digests, and the generators. No real client runs.
tiers.nightly: Run the unlicensed real-client lanes against the local-unlicensed profile using the shared fixture.
tiers.release: Re-run the exact candidate image across every required lane, with fresh licensed overlays for entitlement-bound clients.

receiptBindings.rule: A receipt binds the revisions of the profile it ran against. Until the convergence gaps close, a verifier accepts either the per-file value recorded in currentValues or the composite revision it converges to, and accepts nothing else.

exceptions.reason: OGC CITE suites retain their specification-mandated custom seed and setup procedures.
exceptions.rule: A CITE run shares exact candidate identity, image digest, authentication policy, and capability mapping with release certification, and is never relabelled as having used the canonical client fixture.

outOfScope.statement: Exhaustive geometry, schema, raster, topography, cloud-native, and 3D fixture depth is 2026.2 expansion work tracked by honua-server#3435. Its absence is recorded here as governed gaps and must not block the 2026.1 core.

gaps.reason: No MultiPoint, MultiLineString, or MultiPolygon geometry exists in any canonical fixture input: client-compat-v1.sql seeds only POINT literals and browser-compat.yaml seeds single-part LINESTRING and POLYGON literals.
No polygon with an interior ring is seeded, so ring-order and hole-preservation fidelity is unproven for every client.

Every seeded attribute value is ASCII; the only non-ASCII byte in client-compat-v1.sql is inside a SQL comment. Unicode round-trip through the attribute path is therefore not certified by this fixture.

LineString and Polygon coverage lives on browser_compat layers 2001/2002, whose only fields are objectid, name, and shape. The canonical service test_service layer 0 is Point-only, so no single collection carries both the geometry-type spread and the attribute-type spread.

The py-owslib lane certifies WFS-T insert, update, and delete only on dedicated scratch layers 10-12. No active lane mutates canonical layer 0, and the other advertised Create/Update/Delete/Sync protocol surfaces remain uncertified.

honua.raster_data is seeded only for browser_compat layer 2000. The res-image-layer-0 resource on test_service exists in the Metadata v2 graph with no raster rows behind it, so ImageServer, WCS, and OGC API Coverages on the canonical service have no deterministic content.

Every seeded resource declares styleResourceIds as an empty array, so CERT-RNDR-URL-01 and CERT-RNDR-SYM/LIN/FIL are certified against client-side defaults and Esri drawingInfo derived at request time rather than against a stored, content-addressed style document.

The Portal facade projects only Feature/Map/Image Service items from the seeded services. No Web Map or Dashboard item type is seeded, so the map/dashboard client input named by honua-server#3393 is limited to service items.

The cli lane's OData certification producer (tests/dotnet/Honua.Protocols.OData.Tests/Source/ODataClientCertificationTests.cs) runs in-process against tests/seed/odata.yaml, so its envelope cannot bind this manifest's fixtureRevision.

Two of the five active lanes run their query, schema, and geometry facets against browser_compat layer 2000 rather than the canonical vector service: the js lane through HONUA_SERVICE_ID/HONUA_LAYER_ID and the arcgis-stub lane through ARCGIS_STUB_SERVICE_NAME/ARCGIS_STUB_LAYER_ID. That layer holds three point features and only objectid, name, and shape, so those lanes do not exercise the canonical attribute-type spread, the null geometry, or the ten-feature pagination shape.

The js lane discovers its OGC API Features collection (preferring the configured layer id but falling back to the first collection) and its WFS feature type (the first one that returns features) instead of binding a pinned identity, so a change to the frozen identities would not fail that lane.

tests/python/shared/cert_envelope.py binds fixture_revision to the SHA-256 of tests/seed/client-compat-v1.sql alone and server_config_revision to the SHA-256 of tests/config/client-compat-server-v1.json alone, rather than to the composite fixtureRevision and serverConfigRevision this manifest publishes.
No producer emits auth_policy_revision and fixturePolicy.requiredReceiptFields does not require it, so the auth-policy binding this manifest publishes is not yet enforced on receipts.

The committed .cert.json baselines under tests/baselines/client-compat carry no fixture_revision or server_config_revision field, so the currently active lanes cannot be verified against this manifest until they are re-baselined.
No fixture mints a genuinely expired credential; the closest evidence is the oauth2 refresh_token invalid-grant arm.
portal_private realizes the insufficient-role condition (role portal-admin is granted to no principal) but no 2026.1 case id asserts that a named-user token is refused the private tier.
The client-compat stack provisions a single tenant, so cross-tenant denial cannot be exercised.
Only the admin principal is provisioned, so a separate proposer and approver cannot be represented.
Entitlement-bound access is only realizable on the licensed release overlay; the unlicensed local profile has no entitlement to present.
The unlicensed local profile serves plain HTTP on a private docker network, so CERT-CONN-02 (TLS handshake) is recorded not-applicable there and is certified only by the exact-candidate profile.

docker/client-compat/compose.yml carries the runtime auth settings (HONUA_ADMIN_PASSWORD, Authentication__PortalToken__RequireHttps) alongside the per-lane service definitions, so it is referenced by name rather than digested: every lane addition would otherwise churn serverConfigRevision. The auth-relevant settings are instead pinned by name in authPolicy and digested into authPolicyRevision.

pythonProjection.digestExemptionReason: The Python projection is compared symbol by symbol rather than by digest, so a comment or docstring edit does not force a manifest revision while a value change still fails the drift test.
